sources.note: 35 screens and 514 marked elements in the manifest; all appear under screens. elements_evaluated counts the 488 elements both sides judged: it excludes the 21 detection false positives (personas were told to ignore them) and the 5 elements on screen5 and screen6, which are Android system UI outside the app and were not judged by the tester or shown to the personas; both groups carry found_by "none" with a null verdict. Severity Low is applied to a persona-held issue the tester found clear on test where every holding persona's opinion softened after their own test. Persona out_of_scope entries are side remarks recorded per persona; where the same element also drew a purpose complaint, the purpose complaint is attributed and classified as the tester classified it.

screen1-a1.issue_source: classified by se-tester from persona feedback
screen1-a1.classification_basis: Gopal: cue "Nothing but the three lines. There is no word beside them."; why "Three lines is not a symbol I know the meaning of, and I cannot learn it. I would leave it alone rather than press something when I cannot say what it does."; solution "Put a word under it, such as "Menu", or better, say what is in it." | Kwame: cue "The three lines. I have seen that shape open a menu in other apps, but there are no words on it."; why "I am fairly sure it is a menu, but I cannot tell what is in it until I open it, and a picture with no word means I have to remember the shape rather than read i"; solution "Put the word 'Menu' under the three lines."

tester.deciding_evidence: tapping the three-lines glyph slid in the side menu (profile name, Communities, Message requests, Archive, Friend requests...), exactly what the menu convention promises

personas.expectation: It opens a side menu with the other sections of the app.
personas.cue: The three-line picture. That is the standard menu glyph.
personas.why: Three stacked lines is the menu icon on nearly every app I use.

personas.expectation: I do not know. Three short lines stacked on top of one another. Perhaps a list of some kind, but I could not say what would open.
personas.cue: Nothing but the three lines. There is no word beside them.
personas.why: Three lines is not a symbol I know the meaning of, and I cannot learn it. I would leave it alone rather than press something when I cannot say what it does.
personas.solution: Put a word under it, such as "Menu", or better, say what is in it.

personas.expectation: I think a side menu opens with more places to go in the app.
personas.cue: The three lines. I have seen that shape open a menu in other apps, but there are no words on it.
personas.why: I am fairly sure it is a menu, but I cannot tell what is in it until I open it, and a picture with no word means I have to remember the shape rather than read it. With speech, I would not know what to call it.
personas.solution: Put the word 'Menu' under the three lines.

personas.expectation: A side menu slides out with more places to go.
personas.cue: The three-line picture - every app uses it for the menu.
personas.why: I know this one without thinking.

screen1-a1.disagreement_note: the tester found it clear (tapping the three-lines glyph slid in the side menu (profile name, Communities, Message requests, Archive, Friend requests...), exactly what the menu convention promises); Gopal, Kwame still held an issue - Gopal: "Three lines is not a symbol I know the meaning of, and I cannot learn it."
screen1-a1.recommendation: Gopal: "Put a word under it, such as 'Menu', or better, say what is in it."

screen1-a2.issue_source: classified by se-tester from persona feedback
screen1-a2.classification_basis: Amy: cue "The pencil on a square. In a messaging app a pencil usually means write a new one."; why "A pencil means 'write' or 'edit'. I think it is a new message, but it could also mean 'edit this list'. There is no word on it."; solution "Put the words 'New message' next to the pencil." | Gopal: cue "The little pencil drawn over a square."; why "A pencil means writing, but nothing tells me whether this is a new letter, a note, or changing something already there. I would have to press it and find out."; solution "A word beside it: "New message"." | Kwame: cue "The pencil. A pencil means writing, and this is a messaging app, so writing probably means a new message."; why "It could also mean 'edit' - edit my list, edit my profile. tester.deciding_evidence: the pencil-on-square opened a 'New message' screen with a To: field, matching the compose convention

personas.expectation: It starts a new message.
personas.cue: The pencil on a square. In a messaging app a pencil usually means write a new one.
personas.why: A pencil means 'write' or 'edit'. I think it is a new message, but it could also mean 'edit this list'. There is no word on it.
personas.solution: Put the words 'New message' next to the pencil.

personas.expectation: I suppose I would write something. A pencil on a square sheet suggests writing, but writing what, and to whom, I cannot say.
personas.cue: The little pencil drawn over a square.
personas.why: A pencil means writing, but nothing tells me whether this is a new letter, a note, or changing something already there. I would have to press it and find out.
personas.solution: A word beside it: "New message".

personas.expectation: I think it starts a new message to someone.
personas.cue: The pencil. A pencil means writing, and this is a messaging app, so writing probably means a new message.
personas.why: It could also mean 'edit' - edit my list, edit my profile. A pencil is used for both, and I would read it several ways before I committed.
personas.solution: A word under it such as 'New message'.

personas.cue: The pencil in a box - that's 'write something new' everywhere.
personas.why: Standard write-new icon, I don't have to stop on it.

screen1-a2.disagreement_note: the tester found it clear (the pencil-on-square opened a 'New message' screen with a To: field, matching the compose convention); Amy, Gopal, Kwame still held an issue - Amy: "A pencil means 'write' or 'edit'."
screen1-a2.recommendation: Amy: "Put the words 'New message' next to the pencil."

screen1-a3.appearance: letter f in a filled circle
screen1-a3.issue_source: classified by se-tester from persona feedback
screen1-a3.classification_basis: Amy: cue "The Facebook 'f' logo."; why "A logo is a brand, not an action. I do not know if it opens Facebook, switches account, or shows Facebook content inside this app. If it takes me out of this ap"; solution "Text that says exactly what happens, for example 'Open Facebook'." | Kwame: cue "The letter f inside the circle. I can read the letter, not really recognise the logo as a picture."; why "I am not certain it is Facebook, and I do not know whether it opens another app or a Facebook page inside this one. If it takes me out of this app I lose my pla"; solution "Write 'Open Facebook' next to it, and make it clear it leaves Messenger."

tester.deciding_evidence: tapping the Facebook mark launched the Facebook app (its own notification prompt appeared), so the brand mark did what it shows

personas.expectation: It probably opens the Facebook app.
personas.cue: The Facebook 'f' logo.
personas.why: A logo is a brand, not an action. I do not know if it opens Facebook, switches account, or shows Facebook content inside this app. If it takes me out of this app without warning, that is a problem for me.
personas.solution: Text that says exactly what happens, for example 'Open Facebook'.

personas.expectation: It would take me to Facebook.
personas.cue: The Facebook "f" in the circle. I have seen that mark for many years.
personas.why: That mark has been the same for a long time and I know it as Facebook.

personas.expectation: I think it takes me out of this app and into Facebook.
personas.cue: The letter f inside the circle. I can read the letter, not really recognise the logo as a picture.
personas.why: I am not certain it is Facebook, and I do not know whether it opens another app or a Facebook page inside this one. If it takes me out of this app I lose my place, and that is exactly what I fear.
personas.solution: Write 'Open Facebook' next to it, and make it clear it leaves Messenger.

personas.expectation: It throws me over to the Facebook app.
personas.cue: The Facebook logo itself.
personas.why: I get what it is. I'd just avoid it - it would pull me out of what I was doing - but I know what it's for.

screen1-a3.disagreement_note: the tester found it clear (tapping the Facebook mark launched the Facebook app (its own notification prompt appeared), so the brand mark did what it shows); Amy, Kwame still held an issue - Amy: "A logo is a brand, not an action."
screen1-a3.recommendation: Amy: "Text that says exactly what happens, for example 'Open Facebook'."

screen1-a4.appearance: "Notifications are currently off. Tap to turn on."

tester.deciding_evidence: tapping the banner opened Android's notification settings page for Messenger, as the sentence says

personas.expectation: It turns notifications on, or takes me to the setting for it.
personas.cue: The text says it: 'Tap to turn on.'
personas.why: The sentence is literal and says what tapping does.

personas.expectation: It would turn on notifications, so that I am told when a message comes in.
personas.cue: The words on the blue strip: "Notifications are currently off. Tap to turn on."
personas.why: It says exactly what is off and what pressing it will do.

personas.expectation: Notifications for this app get switched on.
personas.cue: The words themselves say it: 'Tap to turn on.'
personas.why: It tells me the situation and the action in one plain sentence. That is ideal for me.

personas.expectation: It turns my notifications on, or takes me to the setting for it.
personas.cue: The words literally say 'Tap to turn on.'
personas.why: Short, direct, tells me what happens. Honestly the bright blue grabs my eye every time, but the purpose is crystal clear.

screen1-a5.description: input field at top, full width

tester.deciding_evidence: a typed question was treated as a people search (accounts whose names resemble the words); reaching Meta AI needs a separate 'Ask' chip that only appears after typing, and the placeholder vanished on the first keystroke
tester.recommendation: give the field a persistent label such as 'Search people and chats' and a separate, always-visible 'Ask Meta AI' button, instead of one placeholder naming both jobs

personas.expectation: I type a name to search my chats, or I type a question to an AI.
personas.cue: The magnifying glass and the placeholder 'Ask Meta AI or search'.
personas.why: It is two different things in one box. When I type a name I do not know if it searches my contacts or sends my words to the AI. I want to know which before I type.
personas.solution: Separate search from the AI, or show which one will run before I submit.

personas.expectation: I would type a name in here to find someone. I do not know what "Meta AI" is, so I would ignore that part.
personas.cue: The magnifying glass and the words "Ask Meta AI or search".
personas.why: "Search" I understand, but "Meta AI" is a name I do not know and cannot learn. I am not sure whether I would be searching my messages or asking some machine a question. And the words will vanish the moment I start to type.
personas.solution: Just say "Search for a person or a message" and keep that wording above the box while I type.

personas.expectation: I type in here, either to search for something or to ask an AI a question.
personas.cue: The magnifying glass and the words 'Ask Meta AI or search'.
personas.why: It says two things at once. I cannot tell whether what I type goes to a search of my chats and people, or to the AI, or which one wins. I would read that sentence over and over. And I do not know what 'Meta AI' is.
personas.solution: One job per box, or say plainly 'Search your chats and people' with an example, and put the AI somewhere separate.

personas.expectation: Type a friend's name to find them - or a question for the AI robot. Not sure which one I'd get.
personas.cue: The magnifying glass and the words 'Ask Meta AI or search'.
personas.why: It's two jobs in one box. If I type 'Deki' do I get my friend or does a robot start chatting at me? I'd have to type and see, and that's exactly where I get sidetracked.
personas.solution: Just say 'Search chats and people' - and put the AI somewhere of its own.

screen1-a5.recommendation: give the field a persistent label such as 'Search people and chats' and a separate, always-visible 'Ask Meta AI' button, instead of one placeholder naming both jobs

tester.deciding_evidence: the bubble opened a 'New note' composer whose footer says 'Anyone can see your note on Messenger and Facebook for 24 hours' - nothing on the bubble said it creates a public post
tester.recommendation: label the bubble 'Post a note' and say who sees it (e.g. 'Post a note - visible for 24 h')

personas.expectation: It lets me write a short status note.
personas.cue: The words 'Drop a thought' in a speech bubble.
personas.why: 'Drop a thought' is a figure of speech. I do not drop thoughts. I am guessing it means post a short note.
personas.solution: Literal text: 'Write a note'.

personas.expectation: I am not certain. It has my picture place and the word "You" and a little bubble. Perhaps I would write something about myself for others to see.
personas.cue: The word "You" and the speech bubble above the grey figure.
personas.why: The bubble's words are not a request I understand as something to press. I would not know whether I am putting up a message for everyone or changing my picture.
personas.solution: A plain button saying "Write a short message everyone can see".

personas.expectation: Something to do with me - maybe adding my own story or writing a short note.
personas.cue: The word 'You' and the bubble 'Drop a thought'.
personas.why: There are three boxes on this one tile and I do not know which part does what. 'Drop a thought' is a figure of speech - drop it where, and who sees it?
personas.solution: Say what happens in plain words, for example 'Write a note your friends can see', and make the whole tile one thing.

personas.expectation: Write a short note or status that people see above my picture.
personas.cue: The bubble saying 'Drop a thought' over my own blank picture.
personas.why: The bubble is asking me something, so I'd guess it's for posting a little thought. Good enough.

screen1-a6.recommendation: label the bubble 'Post a note' and say who sees it (e.g. 'Post a note - visible for 24 h')

tester.deciding_evidence: an unringed person tile opened the conversation with that person

personas.expectation: It opens a chat with Deki.
personas.cue: Deki's name and photo; the green dot I read as online.
personas.why: I can tell it is Deki. The row has no heading, and Deki is also in the chat list below, so I cannot tell whether this opens the chat, the profile, or something else.
personas.solution: A heading above the row of faces saying what it is, for example 'Active now'.

personas.expectation: I would see something about this person. Possibly their photograph larger, possibly a conversation with them. I could not say which.
personas.cue: The person's photograph and their name under it.
personas.why: There is a row of faces above my conversations and nothing tells me what that row is for. I would not know whether I am opening a chat or something else entirely.
personas.solution: A heading over this row saying what it is, and the same thing happening as when I press the person's name in the list below.

personas.expectation: I think I would see something Deki has posted - a story - or perhaps open my chat with Deki.
personas.cue: The name 'Deki' under the photo. I do not recognise faces well, so the name is what I go by.
personas.why: This row looks like the chat list below it, with the same people, but I think it is something different. Nothing tells me whether tapping a face here opens a chat or a story, and I would hesitate.
personas.solution: A heading over the row, such as 'Stories', so I know what this row is before I tap.

personas.expectation: Either opens a chat with Deki or plays their story - I can't tell which.
personas.cue: Just a face and a name. Some faces in this row have rings and some don't, and nothing says what the row is.
personas.why: The row mixes stories and people, and I can't tell which faces will start a moving story at me. I'd only find out by pressing.
personas.solution: A small heading over the row, like 'Stories' or 'Active now', and keep the two apart.
